dedupe_keys.name: cooper netlogo model of flood damage propagation through a cooperative farming and winemaking system

description: COOPER simulates how flood damage spreads through a cooperative agricultural production system, using winemaking as the example. It was written by David Nortes Martínez in NetLogo with R and published in the CoMSES library (version 1.0.1, 2019). The model couples two environments: a biophysical one covering plant cycles, soil productivity, yield growth and floods, and a productive one covering the social, productive and economic functioning of the system. They are linked by a cooperative made of vineyards, grape-growing farms and cooperative wineries, so damage to vineyards propagates into the wineries' supply. The code is available as a free download from CoMSES under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: it is built around one type of cooperative, and the page does not name the calibration region or give validation. Coverage is general for cooperative farming systems. Simulation uses: estimating indirect flood losses along an agri-food supply chain, beyond direct crop damage. Related records: the food supply chain resilience model (model-comses-food-supply-chain-resilience-efficiency) treats disruption of producer and trader networks more generally.
inputs: Vineyards, vine-growing farms and cooperative wineries
